question: A 12-year-old girl is admitted with right orbital cellulitis following sinusitis. CT orbit shows a well-defined subperiosteal collection medially displacing the medial rectus and globe laterally. She has mild proptosis, restricted medial gaze, and vision 6/6. According to Chandler's classification, this is BEST categorised as:

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Chandler Class I is preseptal — lid oedema without post-septal involvement, proptosis, or restricted motility. The presence of a subperiosteal collection with globe displacement and restricted gaze clearly indicates post-septal disease.

answers.text: Chandler Class II — Orbital cellulitis without abscess

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Chandler Class II involves diffuse post-septal orbital fat inflammation (orbital cellulitis) without a discrete abscess collection. The CT description here shows a well-defined subperiosteal collection — a discrete fluid collection — making this Class III.

Correct. Chandler Class III is defined by a subperiosteal abscess — a collection of pus between the periorbita and the orbital wall, most commonly arising from the medial wall (ethmoid sinusitis). It displaces the periorbita and orbital contents, causing proptosis and restricted gaze. Management: IV antibiotics; surgical drainage is required if vision is threatened, the child is <9 years old with a large medial collection, or if no improvement within 24–48 h.

Chandler Class IV is an orbital abscess within the orbital fat (intraconal or extraconal), not a subperiosteal collection. It is associated with severe proptosis, complete ophthalmoplegia, and high risk of visual loss — more severe than the presentation described here. Class IV almost always requires surgical drainage.

overallFeedback.feedback: Chandler's 5 classes: I (preseptal oedema) → II (orbital cellulitis, no abscess) → III (subperiosteal abscess) → IV (orbital abscess) → V (cavernous sinus thrombosis). A well-defined collection between periorbita and orbital wall displacing the globe = Class III subperiosteal abscess.

Correct — Chandler Class III (subperiosteal abscess). The 5 classes: I = preseptal oedema; II = orbital cellulitis; III = subperiosteal abscess; IV = orbital abscess; V = cavernous sinus thrombosis. Class III–V are post-septal and increasingly require surgical drainage.
